messages.author: be5831679f44e5dc
messages.subject: phylogeny from VCF file
parts:
Hi Everyone,

Just wondering if there was any ideas on how to go from a VCF file (e.g. out of stacks), through dartR filtering, to exporting to a fasta for phylogenetic analyses.

We need the actual REF/SNP as well as the "trimmed sequence" columns for the gl2fasta, but I'm unsure how to create that (or if it's possible to) from a VCF file.

Instructions and/or code would be greatly appreciated.

Thanks,

Renee

messages.author: 9e12eec50c435b60
messages.subject: Re: [dartR] phylogeny from VCF file
parts:
Did you try gl.read.vcf | gl.compliance.check | gl2fasta? Might have to add the trimmed sequences in as a separate exercise. Not sure if they transfer over.

Also note that the development version of dartR.base has a new script gl2snapper. I think concatenating the sequence tags might be problematic -- refer Adam Leache -- if that is what you are planning.

Arthur

messages.author: 9e12eec50c435b60
messages.subject: Re: [dartR] phylogeny from VCF file
parts:
Hi Oumar,

If you have a genlight object already, presumably produced by DArT, you may find that it does not include a trimmedsequence field in the locus metadata. DArT have only recently been generating this as  routine.

So you would have a couple of options. 1. Ask DArT to regenerate your report with trimmed sequences included; or 2. Trim 6 bp off the end of the Sequences. You will lose a bit of data this way, because not all of the sequence will have adaptor residues.

Then use gl2fasta to generate your fastA file.

See how that goes. ☺️

messages.subject: Re: [dartR] phylogeny from VCF file
parts:
Hi All,

Great conversation. I think the challenge is twofold. First, we need to convert the 0/1 SNP data into nucleotides, and then need to be able to output a fasta without calling the trimmed sequences as these are not readily available if you do your own SNP calling in stacks or the like.

When I have time I’ll have think. We should be able to get the Ref/Alt out of the VCF (stacks outputs this as standard), I just need to figure out if/where that info is read into the genlight and stored when a VCF is read through. Then perhaps we can expand the function with a modifier that doesn’t require the trimmed sequence when the origin was a VCF, and output a FASTA with the nucleotides. This is all we would need to be able to run IQtree with the ascertainment bias correction.

Time is the issue! This actually seems like it could be a straightforward hack of the current gl2fasta function.

Thanks,

Renee

messages.author: 592079bda2cb3220
messages.subject: Re: [dartR] phylogeny from VCF file
parts:
Hi Renee,

Something like this:

# installing developing version of dartR
devtools::install_github("green-striped-gecko/dartR@dev")
library(dartR)
# reading vcf
t1 <- gl.read.vcf(system.file('extdata', 'test.vcf', package = 'dartR'))
# SNP nucleotides
t1$loc.all
# removing loci that are not SNPs
# this filtering is performed within the function but include here just for
# testing purposes
no_SNP <- which(nchar(t...@loc.all) >3 )
t1 <- gl.drop.loc(t1,loc.list = locNames(t1)[no_SNP])
t1 <- gl.filter.monomorphs(t1)

t2 <- t1[,1:10]
as.matrix(t2)
t...@loc.all

# method 4: the heterozygous state is resolved by randomly assigning one or
# the other SNP variant to the individual.
gl2fasta(t1,
         method = 4,
         trimmed.sequence = FALSE,
         outfile = "output.fasta",
         outpath = getwd())

system(
"./iqtree2  -s output.fasta -m GTR+ASC"
)

# ERROR: For your convenience alignment with variable sites printed to output.fasta.varsites.phy
# ERROR: Invalid use of +ASC because of 19 invariant sites in the alignment

system(
  "./iqtree2  -s output.fasta.varsites.phy -m GTR+ASC"
)

Cheers,
Luis

messages.author: 9e12eec50c435b60
messages.subject: Re: [dartR] phylogeny from VCF file
parts:
Hi Renee and others,

DartR was initially designed to take reports from Diversity Arrays Technology (DArT), which would include trimmed sequences if requested as part of the service. We have expanded capability to include a wider range of data sources, including vcf files. We are pretty happy to continue to expand this capability, but it is likely that we will compartmentalize this as follows.

gl.read.vcf ...... gl.compliance.check ...... [dartR gl.object] ..... gl2fasta ..... [desired fastA file]

If you have generated the sequence tags outside of DArT, or if you do not have trimmed sequences (easy fix in this case is to copy AlleleSequence to TrimmedSequence), and you are happy with a fastA file that only contains the state change at the SNP locus, then I guess it is possible to modify gl2fasta to take the SNP transitions from gl@other$loc.metrics$SNP rather than from the sequence tags.

This is if I have my head around the problem. I am not familiar with the stacks pipeline and the content of a genlight object brought in from a vcf file. If you clarify, we can give this mod a shot.

A

  "./iqtree2  -s output.fasta.varsites.phy -m GTR+ASC"
)

Luis 


On Tuesday 12 December 2023 at 10:31:20 am UTC+10 renee....@gmail.com wrote:
Hi All,

Great conversation. I think the challenge is twofold. First, we need to convert the 0/1 SNP data into nucleotides, and then need to be able to output a fasta without calling the trimmed sequences as these are not readily available if you do your own SNP calling in stacks or the like.

When I have time I’ll have think. We should be able to get the Ref/Alt out of the VCF (stacks outputs this as standard), I just need to figure out if/where that info is read into the genlight and stored when a VCF is read through. Then perhaps we can expand the function with a modifier that doesn’t require the trimmed sequence when the origin was a VCF, and output a FASTA with the nucleotides. This is all we would need to be able to run IQtree with the ascertainment bias correction.

Time is the issue! This actually seems like it could be a straightforward hack of the current gl2fasta function.

Thanks,

Renee

On 11 Dec 2023, at 7:49 pm, Arthur Georges <geo...@aerg.canberra.edu.au> wrote:

Hi Oumar,

If you have a genlight object already, presumably produced by DArT, you may find that it does not include a trimmedsequence field in the locus metadata. DArT have only recently been generating this as  routine.

So you would have a couple of options. 1. Ask DArT to regenerate your report with trimmed sequences included; or 2. Trim 6 bp off the end of the Sequences. You will lose a bit of data this way, because not all of the sequence will have adaptor residues.

Then use gl2fasta to generate your fastA file.

See how that goes. ☺️

Any guidance will much appreciated.

Regards,

Oumar


On Mon, 11 Dec 2023 at 6:36, Arthur Georges
<geo...@aerg.canberra.edu.au> wrote:
Did you try gl.read.vcf | gl.compliance.check | gl2fasta? Might have to add the trimmed sequences in as a separate exercise. Not sure if they transfer over.

Also note that the development version of dartR.base has a new script gl2snapper. I think concatenating the sequence tags might be problematic -- refer Adam Leache -- if that is what you are planning.

Arthur
